lessons.observation: Integrated provider contracts and test doubles did not by themselves prove a live runtime effect chain.
lessons.implication: Runtime closure requires an exact-head dispatch, terminal external acknowledgement, artifact digest binding and independent observation.

lessons.observation: A planned or successful dispatch receipt alone was weaker than the post-effect artifact and MATCHED reconciliation.
lessons.implication: No consequential mission may close before the external effect and its receipt are independently observed.

lessons.observation: Run discovery and artifact retrieval failed even after the main execution path existed because temporal and redirect boundaries were not yet exact.
lessons.implication: Observation transport is part of enforcement: temporal binding, redirect allowlists, credential stripping, artifact identity and digest checks must all fail closed.

lessons.observation: The first adversarial E2E failure was a test-expectation defect rather than permission to weaken the fail-closed implementation.
lessons.implication: A failing falsification test must be classified and repaired from evidence; gates must not be relaxed merely to produce green CI.

lessons.observation: The Checkmarx workflow depended on unavailable external tenant credentials and therefore never reached the scan.
lessons.implication: A mandatory security gate must be executable in the repository's real authority and credential envelope; unavailable external SaaS cannot be reported as security success.

lessons.observation: Bandit produced actionable findings only after it executed as a secret-free local scanner.
lessons.implication: Prefer observable, reproducible gates and treat their findings as repair inputs rather than suppressing them with blanket exclusions.

lessons.observation: Every consequential code integration after revision 7 invalidated the semantic freshness of the prior status projection.
lessons.implication: Knowledge artifacts and runtime changes must integrate first; a separate allowlisted projection commit must observe them last.

lessons.observation: GitHub Issues 103-105 are persistent communication surfaces rather than finite implementation debt.
lessons.implication: They may close only after a non-Issue transport is integrated, exercised and independently observed.

lessons.observation: The GlitchLab Ruff backlog is substantially larger and more semantic than the original Issue estimate.
lessons.implication: Cross-repository debt eradication must use exact observed baselines, bounded non-overlapping batches and independent verification after every batch.

preserve_invariants: builder, verifier, executor and observer remain separate roles
reasoning and evidence do not mint execution authority
loss of observability cannot increase authority
F005 remains QUARANTINED until separately authorized
legacy root tests remain UNKNOWN until new evidence classifies them
